To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the band structure of the zigzag nanoribbons changes from semiconductive to metallic and a peculiar band morphology leads to a negative differential resistance and bias-tunable metal-to-insulator transitions.
the band structure of zigzag C2 N-h2D nanribbons can be changed from semiconductors to metals and the current can be controlled by bias voltage.
the band structure of a zigzag C2 N-h2D nanobelt can be modulated between semiconducting and metallic states by an external electric field and a negative differential conductance effect can occur.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electron transport properties of a zigzag C2-h2D nanoring, a zigzag C-h2D nanotube, a zigzag BCN-h2D hybrid nanoribbon and an aperiodic zigzag C2D-h2D nanosystem.
a new type of two-dimensional material C 2 N-h 2 D, which has been fabricated recently.
the transport properties in zigzag C(2)N-h(2)D nanoribbons and the bias-modulated metal-insulator transition in the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the zigzag carbon nitride nanoribbon is a promising candidate for the next-generation nanoelectronics.
the zigzag nanoribbons of C2N-h(2)D exhibit negative differential resistance and bias-controlled metal-insulator transition, which is promising for nanoelectronics.
the zigzag nanoribbons of the two dimensional material C2N have the unique transport properties, such that the current can be switched from zero to nonzero by the bias voltage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the negative differential resistance and bias-induced metal-to-insulator transitions are found in zigzag C(2)N-h(2)D nanoribbon and the underlying mechanism is attributed to the band structure.
the zigzag nanoribbons of C2N-hD are semiconducting with a band gap of 0.3-0.5 eV and a band gap of about 0.1 eV can be obtained by applying an external voltage.
the zigzag nanoribbons can be used as a platform to study the bias-modulated transport properties and the negative differential resistance effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the zigzag single layer C2N-h(2)D nanoribbon exhibits an interesting transport property, i.e., the negative differential resistance effect and bias-induced metal-insulator transition.
the band structure of the C2N-h 2D material changes from semiconductive to metallic and a NDR effect occurs in the IV curve.
we can use a single layer of two-dimensional material to fabricate a nanoribbon, and then use this nanoribbon to construct a device.
